meta.name: Smokehouse Creek Fire
meta.evidence: OBSERVED perimeters and satellite detections; gridded conditions; documented facts. No fire spread is simulated.

admin.dataset: Incident attributes on the perimeter record

gaps: No dated perimeters are published for this fire: the timeline uses satellite detections only.
Satellite detections begin 0.5 hours before the discovery time on the administrative record (2024-02-26T20:16:05Z); the record's time is kept as printed.
656 of 5701 detections lie more than 2 km outside this fire's final perimeter: other fires were burning in the same area. They are kept and marked, not removed.

perimeter.provider: National Interagency Fire Center (NIFC) Open Data
perimeter.license: U.S. Government interagency data; provided without warranty
perimeter.caveat: Simplified by the server to about 56 m for display. NIFC: perimeters are 'not better than the original sources from which they were derived'.

detections.provider: NASA FIRMS (LANCE), VIIRS 375 m active fire product
detections.caveat: FIRMS: each detection 'represents the center of a pixel flagged as containing one or more fires'; 'the location is the center point of the pixel (not necessarily the coordinates of the actual fire)'. Smoke, cloud and the gaps between overpasses hide fire.

gridmet.provider: Climatology Lab, University of California Merced (gridMET; Abatzoglou 2013)
gridmet.dataset: Daily 4-km surface meteorology and fire danger indices, point series at the ignition point
gridmet.license: Copyright waived by the author (public domain dedication)
gridmet.caveat: A gridded estimate, not a station observation. gridMET: wind fields 'are interpolated from NARR/NLDAS-2 which has a 32-km spatial resolution. This will be insufficient for capturing mesoscale influences of terrain on wind fields.'

power.provider: NASA Langley Research Center, POWER project (MERRA-2)
power.dataset: Daily point data: WS10M_MAX, RH2M, T2M_MAX, PRECTOTCORR
power.caveat: About half a degree of latitude by five eighths of a degree of longitude: a regional value, not conditions at the fire front.

drought.provider: U.S. Drought Monitor (NDMC, USDA, NOAA, NASA)
drought.license: Authorized for use with attribution: 'The U.S. Drought Monitor is jointly produced by the National Drought Mitigation Center at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, the U.S. Department of Agriculture, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and NASA. Data courtesy of NDMC.'

gasPipelines.dataset: Natural gas interstate and intrastate pipelines (map layer shapefile)
gasPipelines.caveat: A schematic national layer: positions are approximate.

transmission.provider: Homeland Infrastructure Foundation-Level Data (HIFLD), archived copy
transmission.dataset: U.S. Electric Power Transmission Lines (Archive), last data update 30 September 2024
transmission.license: Redistribution terms of the archived copy were not verified; only derived counts and lengths are stored, not the lines
transmission.caveat: The layer describes the grid as of its last update, not on the day of the fire.

facts.label: Size
facts.quote: the Smokehouse Creek Fire—the largest wildfire in Texas history that originated near Stinnett, Texas, in February 2024 and burned 1,054,153 acres

facts.label: Ignition
facts.value: A power pole broke and its line fell into grass, 26 February 2024
facts.quote: a decayed power pole broke at ground level and caused the three-wire power line atop it to fall and make contact with fine grassy fuels, igniting what would become the Smokehouse Creek Fire
facts.source: Texas House of Representatives, Investigative Committee on the Panhandle Wildfires, report

facts.label: Cause, as found by the committee
facts.value: Downed power poles owned by Xcel Energy
facts.quote: Both the Smokehouse Creek and Reamer Creek fires were caused by downed power poles owned by Xcel Energy
facts.source: Texas House of Representatives, Investigative Committee on the Panhandle Wildfires, report

facts.label: Spread
facts.value: About 40,000 acres on 27 February, more than 900,000 two days later
facts.quote: Approximately 40,000 acres burned on February 27th, expanding to more than 900,000 acres over the next two days
facts.source: Texas House of Representatives, Investigative Committee on the Panhandle Wildfires, report

facts.label: Losses
facts.value: More than 15,000 cattle; an estimated 138 homes and businesses
facts.quote: More than 15,000 head of cattle (including pregnant cows) perished, an estimated 138 homes and businesses were destroyed, and over one million acres of land were consumed
facts.source: Texas House of Representatives, Investigative Committee on the Panhandle Wildfires, report

facts.label: Costs to utilities
facts.value: The committee expects utilities may seek to pass costs on
facts.quote: it is anticipated that utility companies may seek to pass along the costs of electrical infrastructure repairs and damages paid to landowners for fire-related losses
facts.source: Texas House of Representatives, Investigative Committee on the Panhandle Wildfires, report
